title: Measure whether anonymity and the blind first pass change anything
question: Do anonymity and a blind independent first pass alter the outcome distribution, or are they ceremony? Matched councils: identity revealed versus concealed; round-1 position independence, anchoring on a high-status first speaker, and final-verdict divergence.
answer: Anonymity plus a blind independent first pass alter round-1 position independence and first-speaker anchoring relative to identity-revealed sequential speaking with a high-status first speaker; final verdicts also diverge on a substantial share of matched seeds. n=24 matched seeds. Independence delta (concealed-revealed) mean=0.424415 95% bootstrap CI [0.421694, 0.426976] Cohen d_z=64.05249058538976. Anchoring pull delta (revealed-concealed) mean=0.539264 95% CI [0.534898, 0.543368] Cohen d_z=48.95387126639008. Final-verdict disagreement rate mean=0.333333 95% CI [0.166667, 0.500000]. Name-masking without a blind first pass (ceremony control) matches the revealed arm on independence. SUCCESS:TST-0289
finding_plain: Anonymity plus a blind independent first pass alter round-1 position independence and first-speaker anchoring relative to identity-revealed sequential speaking with a high-status first speaker; final verdicts also diverge on a substantial share of matched seeds.
